Both versions check out. Here are the two ways to reuse existing tags — they're identical apart from the tag-suggestion behavior. I've pre-loaded three example bookmarks in each so there are existing tags (*reading, sleep, work, reference, cli, design*) to draw on.

**Version A — a dropdown you click**
→ http://maker:4001/tags-a.html

Try this: paste `https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/01/well/sleep-habits.html`, click **Get details**, then in the **Tags** field type `re`. A little list should drop down showing your matching existing tags (*reading*, *reference*). **Click "reference"** to add it.

**Version B — inline autocomplete you accept with a key**
→ http://maker:4001/tags-b.html

Try this: same steps, but when you type `re` in the **Tags** field, the rest of a matching tag (*reading*) appears greyed right inside the field, with a hint below. **Press the Tab key** to accept it.

Both suggest only from tags you already have, so you stay consistent, and both still let you type a brand-new tag normally (just keep typing and add a comma).

One choice I made in both, so it's visible: **suggestions match anywhere in the tag in Version A (so "re" also finds "reference"), while Version B completes from the start of the word.** 

Try each and tell me **which one feels better to you** — or if a mix of the two is closer to what you'd want. Whichever you pick becomes how tag reuse works.
